channel.tool.message.description: Ask one participant of this task a short question and get their reply back as the result. Use it for a quick input: a fact, a confirmation, a choice. Name the participant in "to" by the id shown in the list of participants. Do not use it to hand over work: for work a participant must do, use create_task_for_participant. If an agent answers with a question of its own, reply by calling again with the taskId it gave you.
channel.tool.message.conversation: "{participant}" is reached on this task's own conversation. Put the question to them with ask_user.
channel.tool.task.description: Give one participant of this task a piece of work to do as a task of their own, and wait for its outcome. Use it when the participant must do something — investigate, produce, change. Do not use it for a quick question: for that, use message_participant. Name the participant in "to" by the id shown in the list of participants. They start with no context: put everything they need in the message and say what done means in acceptanceCriteria. The task is recorded as a sub-task of this one. If the participant asks a question about the work, answer by calling again with the taskId given. Only an agent participant can be given a task; a user is asked with message_participant.
channel.tool.task.conversation: "{participant}" is reached only on this task's own conversation and cannot be given a task of their own. Ask them with message_participant instead.

cli.usage:
Usage:
  yaah [--config <path>]          Start a harness and chat with it in the terminal.
  yaah serve [--config <path>]    Start a harness and serve the A2A API and the web UI.
  yaah tui --url <harness>        Chat in the terminal with a harness that is already running.

Options:
  --config <path>   Use this configuration file instead of ~/.yaah/config.toml.
  -h, --help        Show this help.
  -v, --version     Show the version.
